intro: Dark whispers fill the library. Clear four chambers of lore to see through Ganonix's disguises, then break the final ward.

trials.title: The Leaky Scroll
trials.prompt: This config file is about to be committed. Flag every line that should never be in source code.
trials.hint: Passwords and access keys belong in a secret manager, not in the repository.
trials.success: Two secrets caught before they reach Git history. Keep them in a vault.

trials.title: Wards and Their Weaknesses
trials.prompt: Pair each security control with the threat it guards against.
trials.hint: Think about what each tool looks at: commits, packages, source code, merges, or permissions.
trials.success: Each ward is bound to its threat.

pairs.right: Opens pull requests for vulnerable packages
Finds vulnerabilities in your source code
Gives a workflow only the access it needs

trials.title: The Leak Ritual
trials.prompt: A key just leaked. Put the response steps in the right order.
trials.hint: Stop the bleeding first. Cleaning up and learning from it come afterwards.
trials.success: Revoke first, then rotate, clean, prevent, and learn.

items.text: Issue a new one and store it in a secret manager
Remove it from the code and Git history
Turn on secret scanning to stop a repeat

trials.title: The Hooded Reviewer
trials.prompt: A pull request bumps a package to a version from an unknown fork. Tests are green. What do you do?
trials.hint: Passing tests show the code works. They do not show where the code came from.
trials.success: Wise. Supply chain risk hides behind green checks.

options.why: Green tests do not prove a dependency is trustworthy.

options.text: Run dependency review and verify the package source first.
Turn off dependency review so PRs stop blocking.
options.why: Disabling the check is exactly what Ganonix wants.
